science.title: Epigenetic regulation of cancer drivers and EMT revealed by genome-wide methylome profiling in NSCLC
science.description: Carcinogenesis is driven by dynamic and heterogeneous epigenomic alterations promoting tumour evolution and affecting therapeutic resistance. We performed genome-wide DNA methylation sequencing (RRBS) on 260 lung methylomes from 130 non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) patients. Here we show that gene-body hypomethylation involved lung cancer drivers, while promoter hypomethylation targeted miRNA genes linked to EGFR signalling, EMT, and PD-L1 regulation. Upstream transcription factor analysis also implicated epigenetic control of EMT, EGFR and immune pathways, through SNAIL, SLUG, SMAD3 and BRD4. Promoter hypermethylation represented multi-gene epi-oncodriver mechanism associated with GPCRs. Subtype-specific patterns were additionally observed: adenocarcinoma showed alterations in neurotransmitter signalling, whereas squamous cell carcinoma embraced canonical oncogenic pathways. We provide a genome-wide methylome analysis in NSCLC, revealing epigenetic alterations that may contribute to tumour progression and therapeutic resistance linked to EGFR, EMT and immunological responses. These findings highlight the translational potential of epigenetic profiling to inform clinical strategies in NSCLC.
